review.note: Drafted by the assistant under the owner's dated exception, from the sources named and not from a reading of them; the argument is the thing to check, not only the dates.

explanation: Schengen was an agreement among member states of the European Communities. The states made it outside the Community treaties, and only members were party to it. Portugal had been a member for five years when it signed in 1991. The precondition is institutional. Accession did not make Portugal want an open border with Spain, and Lisbon and Madrid had their own reasons for wanting one. Without accession there would have been nothing for Portugal to sign. Nobody disputes that much, which is why the confidence is `consensus`. The link does not answer why the two Iberian states joined the first wave, when they could have waited to see how it worked.
